summary: Restore ṣ in the Infectum base form
rationale: The root is ṣʕb and the entry itself quotes ko-ṣoʕəb. The corpus at 78/30 likewise has koṣoʕəb. Plain s in the base form is an evident consonant slip.

summary: Translate ʕal an=nišaṯṯe as about their wives
rationale: The quoted Turoyo says d-šəmʕi hawxa mede ʕal an=nišaṯṯe, with ʕal introducing the subject of the words. The corpus at 78/30 has the same reading, and its translation explicitly says so etwas über ihre Frauen hören. From incorrectly makes the wives the source of the words.

after: hart sein; (mit ʕal-) für jemanden schwer zu ertragen sein;
rationale: 78/30 explicitly codes an objectionable matter as subject and affected people with ʕal-. Clarifies the attested experiential difficulty meaning beyond bare hart sein without removing inherited wording or adding an unsupported physical-hardness example.

summary: u medano is the subject of koṣoʕəb; aʕlayye marks the people who find the matter hard to bear. The d-clause specifies hearing such statements about their wives; it is not an external agent.

The edition German über ihre Frauen matches Turoyo ʕal an nišaṯṯe. Inherited English from their wives is not securely equivalent; retain inherited quotation pending translation review rather than silently substituting a new translation.

This single attestation supports the relational difficulty construction. It does not show physical hardness, a new stem or an additional idiom. The existing 78/29–30 citation already covers assigned 78/30.

Review inherited English 'from their wives' against the supplied German 'über ihre Frauen' and Turoyo ʕal an nišaṯṯe. The German edition and Turoyo support 'about' rather than an asserted source of speech.
